blocks.title: Después de este pdf sabrás
bullets: pedir algo con educación con could y can
expresar obligación con must y have to, y conocer la diferencia entre mustn't y don't have to

blocks.text: El imperativo es el verbo sin nada y sin sujeto, igual para tú, usted, vosotros y ustedes: Sit down. Close the door. Be careful! Para negar se pone Don't delante: Don't worry. Don't be late. Con Let's propones algo al grupo: Let's go! (¡Vamos!)

blocks.title: please lo hace educado
blocks.text: Un imperativo inglés suena brusco enseguida. En España Ponme un café es normal; en inglés Give me a coffee suena muy mal. Añade please o usa una pregunta: Could I have a coffee, please? o Could you close the door, please? es mucho más amable que Close the door.

items: Sin -s con he, she e it: She can swim, He must go.
Después va el verbo sin nada, sin to: You should rest, no should to rest.
Preguntas y negaciones sin do: Can you help? You shouldn't smoke.
Excepción: have to funciona como un verbo normal, con do y con -s.

head: Verbo
Significado
Ejemplo
rows: I can drive. Can I sit here?
I could swim when I was five. Could you help me?
May I come in? It may rain.
tener que (una norma o una situación)
I have to wear a uniform at work.
no tener que, no hacer falta

blocks.title: mustn't no es 'no hace falta'
blocks.text: You mustn't go = no debes ir, no puedes ir. You don't have to go = no tienes que ir, no hace falta (pero puedes). Por suerte funciona como en español: no tienes que = don't have to, no debes = mustn't.

blocks.title: had to en el pasado
blocks.text: must no tiene pasado. Usa had to: I had to work late yesterday (ayer tuve que trabajar hasta tarde). Con can: could o was able to.

head: Inglés
Español
rows: Could you speak more slowly, please?
Could I have the bill, please?
Después de should no va to.
Un verbo modal forma la pregunta él solo.
Para ofrecer algo: Would you like, no Do you like.

blocks.text: Completa con el verbo modal o la forma correcta. Las respuestas están en la última página.

items.q: You look ill. You ______ see a doctor.
items.full: You look ill. You should see a doctor.
Could you open the window, please?
You mustn't smoke in the hospital.

items.q: It's Sunday. You ______ get up early.
items.full: It's Sunday. You don't have to get up early.

items.q: She ______ wear a uniform at work.
items.full: She has to wear a uniform at work.

items.q: Yesterday I ______ wait for an hour.
items.full: Yesterday I had to wait for an hour.
Don't worry. It's not a problem.

items.q: When I was young I ______ run very fast.
items.full: When I was young I could run very fast.
Do I have to pay now?

items.q: ______ you like a cup of tea?
items.full: Would you like a cup of tea?

items.q: Ayer tuve que trabajar hasta tarde.
items.a: I had to work late yesterday.
